findings.claim: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), the result of getResourceTypeResource() can be null and is passed to findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. This causes a NullPointerException, which surfaces as HTTP 500 instead of 403. It can also happen when realm admin permissions are disabled after the client exists.

verifier.reason: ClientPermissionsV2.java:217-219 passes the result of getResourceTypeResource() straight to findByResource(), yet AdminPermissionsSchema.java:117-119 returns null whenever realm admin permissions are disabled (toggleable after the fact via updateRealm, DefaultExportImportManager.java:783) while V2 is chosen by feature flag alone (AdminPermissions.java:40) and the admin-permissions client's resource server still exists; StoreFactoryCacheSession.java:938 then dereferences resource.getId() and throws NPE (ClientPermissionsV2.java:224 resource.getScopes() would too). The 500 status is inferred from the uncaught NPE, not executed.

findings.claim: The AdminPermissions role/client/group removal listener is guarded only by the V1 flag ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. When only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, the permission cleanup block is skipped and permission resources are left orphaned.

verifier.reason: The removal listener is wrapped only in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77), so with only V2 enabled the whole block is skipped. No other ClientRemovedEvent handler deletes the per-client V2 resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:93-104); note the skipped block would not have removed them anyway, since ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException (ClientPermissionsV2.java:193-194).

findings.claim: The removal listener is now wrapped in a V1-only feature gate. Deployments without V1 no longer clean up leftover V1 permission resources and policies when a role, client or group is deleted.

verifier.reason: The V1-only gate is real (services/.../permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77), but it removes no cleanup that worked before. With neither feature on, `authz` is null (MgmtPermissions.java:85) so `realmResourceServer()` returns null (MgmtPermissions.java:251) and the delete paths return early (ClientPermissions.java:190, RolePermissions.java:88, GroupPermissions.java:462); with V2 on, the listener already looked in the admin-permissions client's resource server (MgmtPermissionsV2.java:52-54), not the realm-management one that holds V1 data.

findings.claim: Under V2, deleting a client leaves its per-client resource and scope permissions orphaned, because there is no V2 cleanup path.

verifier.reason: The patch gates the only admin-permissions `ClientRemovedEvent` cleanup behind the V1 feature flag (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77,89-91), and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` just throws. The remaining listener (server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/store/syncronization/ClientApplicationSynchronizer.java:49-74) only removes the deleted client's own resource server and client-policy references, so the per-client resource created in the admin-permissions resource server (server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:93-104) and its scope permissions are never removed.

findings.claim: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission uses findByType(server, 'Clients'). This matches only the typed all-clients resource, because per-client resources are created without a type. As a result it never returns per-client IDs and may return the string 'Clients', which callers such as AvailableRoleMappingResource pass to realm.getClientById.

verifier.reason: ClientPermissionsV2.java:138-140 calls findByType(server, "Clients") and adds resource.getName(); the JPA query matches `r.type = :type` exactly (ResourceEntity.java:64), and only the all-clients resource is typed (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:250) while per-client resources are created with no setType (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104). So it can only yield the name "Clients", which AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:230 passes to realm.getClientById(cid).getRolesStream() (null dereference); that caller path is gated on the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ flag (line 217), so it is largely latent under V2-only.

findings.claim: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) looks up the resource with findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()). AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with owner resourceServer.getClientId(), so the lookup never finds them and always falls back to the all-clients resource.

verifier.reason: The owner ids are the same value: `ResourceServer.getClientId()` returns `getId()` in both implementations (model/jpa/.../ResourceServerAdapter.java:91-93, model/infinispan/.../ResourceServerAdapter.java:121-123). So the lookup at ClientPermissionsV2.java:214 (name `client.getId()`, owner `server.getId()`) matches resources created at AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104 (name from `resolveClient` = `client.getId()`, owner `resourceServer.getClientId()`).

findings.claim: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) does not filter on permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()), unlike UserPermissionsV2.java:135.

verifier.reason: ClientPermissionsV2.java:226-232 loops over the evaluated permissions and checks only permission.getScopes(), with no resource-id comparison, whereas UserPermissionsV2.java:135 guards the same loop with permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()). Only a single ResourcePermission for that resource is passed to root.evaluatePermission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:224), so the missing filter looks like a defensive inconsistency; I did not trace the evaluator to confirm it can never return other resources.

findings.claim: ClientPermissionsV2 uses Arrays.asList() for single-element lists where List.of() could be used.

verifier.reason: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:225 and :250 both build `List<String> expectedScopes = Arrays.asList(scope)` from a single `String scope` parameter (methods at :207 and :237), while the same file already uses `List.of(...)` at :268. Purely stylistic; behaviour differs only for a null scope.

findings.claim: There is no migration for realms whose admin-permissions client already existed. Those realms never receive the Clients resource type or the new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite). As a result getResourceTypeResource returns null, and creating a Clients permission fails with 'Scope [configure] does not exist' or 'No scopes found'.

verifier.reason: `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists (server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:224-228) and no migration code references the schema, so pre-existing realms never get the `Clients` resource or the new scopes. `getResourceTypeResource` then returns null from `findByName` (:133), and permission creation throws 'Scope [configure] does not exist.' (:210) or 'No scopes found.' (:108).

findings.claim: Tests access getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) without checking that the list has at least two elements, which risks an IndexOutOfBoundsException.

verifier.reason: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:170-174 asserts only `not(empty())` before calling `defaultClientScopes.get(1)`, so a one-element list would throw IndexOutOfBoundsException. The literal `getDefaultClientScopes().get(1)` at line 148 is harmless (the server's requireView at ClientResource.java:382 should throw ForbiddenException first), and a client created in a realm normally has several default scopes, so this is only a weak-assertion nit in test code.

findings.claim: canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException. When token-exchange and admin-fine-grained-authz:v2 are both enabled, this produces HTTP 500 instead of 403.

verifier.reason: `ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:148-150), and the patch makes `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` return that class (MgmtPermissionsV2.java:64-68). `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:276` calls it uncaught for any audience other than the requesting client, so `KeycloakErrorHandler.java:146` maps it to 500 rather than the 403 on line 280; `token-exchange` v1 has no dependency stopping it being enabled alongside `admin-fine-grained-authz:v2` (Profile.java:76).

findings.claim: The evaluate-and-match-scope loop is duplicated three times: hasGrantedPermission duplicates ClientPermissions.hasPermission(Resource,String), and the two hasPermission overloads repeat the same logic.

findings.claim: Once a per-client permission exists for a client, all-clients permissions stop applying to it. Per-client resources are created without a type, and DefaultPolicyEvaluator adds type-level policies only when resource.getType() != null.

verifier.reason: Per-client resources are created with no type (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104), and ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(client, scope) falls back to the typed "Clients" resource only when no per-client resource exists (ClientPermissionsV2.java:214-222). DefaultPolicyEvaluator.java:71-88 then collects only that resource's own policies, because the type branch is skipped and findByScopes(null resource) requires resource-less policies; so all-clients manage/configure/map-roles grants are dropped for that client (only all-clients VIEW survives, via canView()).

findings.claim: Tests are missing for MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, the client-scope endpoints, realm-management escalation, and V2 delete cleanup.

verifier.reason: The only Clients-type tests are the five in tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java, which grant only MANAGE, CONFIGURE, VIEW, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE (e.g. line 359), so `canMapClientScopeRoles` and the ClientScopeModel checks (ClientPermissionsV2.java:102, 106-122) are never exercised. No test touches the realm-level client-scopes endpoints or realm-management escalation, and the single V2 client delete (PermissionClientTest.java:274) only asserts the client is gone, not that its permission resources are cleaned up.

findings.claim: The Javadoc on the void methods requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() says 'Returns true if...', but these methods throw ForbiddenException and return nothing.

verifier.reason: The patch adds Javadoc reading "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}" on `void requireView()` (ClientPermissionEvaluator.java:95-98) and the equivalent on `void requireViewClientScopes()` (ClientPermissionEvaluator.java:100-103). The implementations return nothing and throw ForbiddenException when the check fails (ClientPermissions.java:292-296, 505-509).

findings.claim: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName has no CLIENTS case and handles only Users, so Clients resources resolve to a null display name.

verifier.reason: `getResourceName` (server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:304-326) branches only on `USERS.getType()` and otherwise returns `resource.getDisplayName()`. Clients resources never get a display name set (created by `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, ...)` at :104, and in `init` at :249-250 with no `setDisplayName`), so it is null for them.

findings.claim: The Javadoc text 'For V2 only: Also if ... for all clients' misdescribes V2 behavior: V2 replaces the V1 per-client check rather than adding to it, and V2 also honours per-client grants.

verifier.reason: The Javadoc matches what V2 does: ClientPermissionsV2.java:207-222 checks a per-client grant first and falls back to the all-clients resource, which is what the per-client sentence plus "For V2 only: Also ... all clients" says (ClientPermissionEvaluator.java:172-174), and the V1 and V2 scope names are identical strings. V2 does override without calling super (ClientPermissionsV2.java:91-93), but that only changes where the grant is stored, not the documented conditions.

findings.claim: An all-clients map-roles grant, or configure plus map-roles-composite, also covers the realm-management client. This lets an admin with map-roles on users grant realm-admin privileges, bypassing checkAdminRoles validation.

verifier.reason: ClientPermissionsV2.java:207-222 falls back to the all-clients resource for any client with no resource of its own, with no exclusion for realm-management, so canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles (lines 91-98) return true for it. RolePermissions.java:308 and :398 then return true before reaching checkAdminRoles (only called at :325 and :415), letting an admin who also has map-roles on a user assign realm-admin.

findings.claim: canView() accepts only the VIEW scope and not MANAGE, so GET /client-scopes returns 403 for admins with only all-clients MANAGE. This is inconsistent with canManageClientScopes() and canView(ClientScopeModel).

verifier.reason: ClientPermissionsV2.java:86-88 makes canView() true only for the view-clients/manage-clients roles or the all-clients VIEW scope, while canManageClientScopes() (106-110) and canView(ClientScopeModel) (118-122) also accept MANAGE. findings.claim: The tests do not clean up after themselves: @AfterEach removes only permissions, testManageOnlyOneClient leaves a renamed client and changed client-scope types, and testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient leaves roles and mappings behind. Results therefore depend on test order.

verifier.reason: The leftover state is real: `onAfter()` at tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:78-83 removes only scope permissions, while the rename and scope move (166-178) and the roles, mapping and composite (334-364) are never reverted, and the framework runs only registered policy-removal tasks on the class-scoped realm (AbstractPermissionTest.java:128-131, test-framework/core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testframework/injection/Registry.java:196-211). The order-dependence is latent only: I found no existing assertion that reads the leaked state, so no test provably changes outcome today.

findings.claim: hasPermission(String) runs a full policy evaluation of the all-clients resource on every call without checking whether any policies exist, causing repeated evaluations per client in GET /clients.

verifier.reason: `hasPermission(String)` at ClientPermissionsV2.java:237-260 calls `root.evaluatePermission` whenever the Clients resource exists, with no policy-existence guard like the one at ClientPermissionsV2.java:219 and no caching across calls (the decision cache is created per `evaluate()` call, UnboundedPermissionEvaluator.java:44).
